- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 82.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above true peak or adjust downward by 1–3% after 2–3 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast slope and avoid sharp downward revisions.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion zones (e.g., below 75.0) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment <0.5.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is clustered above 0.7; apply downward adjustment of 1–4% for 3–5 consecutive days of high sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7×true + 0.3×forecast) for 3–5 day windows.
